title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Tunnel Frame Parser Architecture
purpose: Define the RFC 9220 WebSocket-over-HTTP/3 frame parsing and message reassembly boundary.
design_summary: The WebSocket tunnel parser stays in `Incursa.Quic.Http3` above the QUIC transport runtime and below any future application handler dispatch. `Http3WebSocketMessageReader` incrementally consumes bytes from an RFC 9220 Extended CONNECT stream, validates RSV bits, opcodes, endpoint-role masking policy, payload length encodings, continuation sequencing, control-frame constraints, and complete text-message UTF-8, and surfaces complete unmasked messages. `Http3WebSocketCloseFrameParser` validates transmitted close status codes and UTF-8 close reasons. `Http3WebSocketFrameWriter` provides deterministic frame formatting for local tests, benchmarks, and later adapter work without opening a live tunnel API in this slice.
data_and_state_considerations: The reader owns only per-stream parser state: pending partial frame bytes, an optional fragmented data opcode, and accumulated fragmented payload bytes. It does not create sockets, dispatch application handlers, mutate QUIC stream state, or change HTTP/3 request routing. Payload bytes are copied into completed message records so callers receive stable unmasked data independent of the input buffer lifetime.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The server-side reader requires masked client frames.
The client-side reader rejects masked server frames.
Control frames must be final and no larger than 125 bytes.
Continuation frames require an open fragmented data message.
A stream end with a partial frame or incomplete fragmented message is rejected as malformed tunnel data.
Invalid UTF-8 text messages and close reasons are rejected.
Reserved or partial close status payloads are rejected.
risks: This slice does not add application-level WebSocket handler registration or dispatch.
This slice does not forward tunnel bytes between HTTP/3 streams and TCP sockets.
This slice does not implement close-handshake orchestration.
This slice does not move WebSocket behavior into the QUIC packet, TLS, recovery, or stream runtime.

supplemental_sections.heading: Next Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: A later slice can connect the parser to `Http3Server` request handling for supported `:protocol = websocket` requests. That later work should own handler integration, tunnel lifecycle, close-code policy, and stream forwarding without changing this parser's role-specific wire validation.
